design:privacy-C-cryptographic.recommendation: Proposal for the owner: do not make Family C the core privacy mechanism for the prototype or the production default. Adopt hybrid H1 instead: server-derived per-course pseudonyms (Family A or B) inside an identity-free, pseudonym-keyed data model behind a PseudonymSource interface, so that client-held, blind-signed pseudonyms (C1) can be switched in at a term boundary with no schema change. Take one Family C technique now, blind-signed one-time exit-survey tokens (RFC 9474 / Privacy Pass), along with two separate cookie-less origins, day-coarsened timestamps, and crypto-shredding of K_c (subject to Q17). Exact merge de-duplication (§7.7) requires a per-course linkable pseudonym, so per-question nullifier designs (Semaphore-style) cannot meet the spec.

options.name: C1: blind-signed per-course pseudonym (client-held secret, RFC 9474)
options.verdict: Buildable but not recommended as the default. It meets merges, one upvote per student, counters, rate limiting, pseudonymous bans, and stored-data unlinkability, even against the DB console, dumps and backups. It conflicts with targeted e-mail (§7.13) and the §6.4 exceptional process. It allows undetectable level-token transfer (§7.11) and Sybil pseudonyms through device-loss re-issuance. Its guarantee against the operator holds only if the operator is passive, because the server ships the JS. It could later be an institution-configurable strong-anonymity mode.

options.name: C2: per-question nullifiers (Semaphore v4)
options.verdict: Rejected. Nullifiers are unlinkable across questions, so after a merge the true upvote total is known only to lie between max(a,b) and a+b. That violates 'without double-counting a student' (§7.7). It also brings ZK artifacts and an Ethereum-oriented ecosystem.

options.name: C3: BBS anonymous credentials with client-held counters
options.verdict: Not feasible. It is theoretically the strongest option and fixes level-token transfer. But the blind BBS and per-verifier-linkability drafts are only at -03 (Active RG Documents), core BBS is draft-12 and not an RFC, and I found no mainstream TS implementation of the blind or pseudonym extensions.

options.name: H1 hybrid: server HMAC pseudonym now, C1-ready data model, blind-token survey
options.verdict: Recommended proposal. It keeps the §6.4 option open (K_c under k-of-n custody), supports targeted e-mail through the narrow API, keeps grade integrity, needs no recovery UX, and allows a later upgrade with no schema change.

options.name: Blind-signed exit-survey tokens (any family)
options.verdict: Recommended. It is low effort and gives duplicate prevention with no identity linkage at all, plus no stored timestamp, IP or user agent (§7.12).

key_claims.claim: RFC 9474 (RSA Blind Signatures) is Informational, IRTF CFRG, October 2023; it defines 4 variants, with the Randomized variants RECOMMENDED; it provides blindness and one-more unforgeability; it has no public-metadata support
RFC 9576 says that in the shared Origin/Attester/Issuer model, unlinkability depends on separating issuance and redemption in time or space, and that metadata bits partition the anonymity set
RFC 9578 is Proposed Standard (June 2024) and defines token types 0x0001 VOPRF(P-384) (privately verifiable) and 0x0002 Blind RSA 2048 (publicly verifiable)
The Privacy Pass rate-limit-tokens draft (-06) and the key-consistency drafts have expired; batched-tokens draft-08 is with the IESG; RFC 9577 is Proposed Standard
RFC 9497 OPRF/VOPRF/POPRF is Informational, IRTF, December 2023, and its output is deterministic per key and input
draft-irtf-cfrg-bbs-signatures-12 (2026-09-28) is an Active RG Document with intended status Informational; it has not been published as an RFC
The blind BBS draft (-03, 2026-06-26) and the BBS per-verifier-linkability draft (-03, 2026-06-29) are Active RG Documents
RFC 9458 (Oblivious HTTP) requires that the relay not be operated by the same entity as the gateway
MDN browser-compat-data lists WebAuthn PRF in get() as Chrome 116 and Firefox 139, but Safari false (webkit bug 259934); in create() it lists Safari 18
WebKit says Safari 18.0 adds support for the WebAuthn prf extension, without specifying create() vs get()

@cloudflare/blindrsa-ts 0.4.6, Apache-2.0, has a single runtime dependency (sjcl 1.0.9) and implements RFC 9474 plus the partially-blind draft-02; partially-blind verification does not work in browsers
@cloudflare/voprf-ts is 1.0.0 (BSD-3-Clause); @cloudflare/privacypass-ts is 0.9.0 (Apache-2.0) and claims RFC 9578 compliance
Semaphore v4 nullifiers are derived from the scope plus the user's private key, giving one valid proof per scope; v4.0.0 was audited by PSE and the trusted setup completed on 13 July 2024
@semaphore-protocol/core latest is 4.14.3 (MIT)
Semaphore proof-generation timings and artifact sizes are published only as images
@digitalbazaar/bbs-signatures 3.1.0 (BSD-3-Clause); which draft revision it implements is not stated
Windows Hello support for the WebAuthn PRF extension
Analysis, not a sourced fact: with per-question nullifiers the merged upvote total is only known to lie in [max(a,b), a+b], so exact §7.7 de-duplication needs a per-course linkable pseudonym
The spec requires protection against ordinary queries, instructors, TAs, admins, logs, exports and predictable IDs (§6.2, §9), not against the operator or vendors

new_open_questions: NQ-C1: Is in-app-only delivery, or a content-free uniform daily digest, acceptable for per-question notifications and 'Participation level reached'? Or must each §7.13 event have a targeted e-mail, which requires a server-side event-to-recipient mapping?
NQ-C2: Must anonymity hold against the platform operator and vendors (beyond §6.2)? Does UW require the §6.4 exceptional deanonymization process? The two answers pull in opposite directions.
NQ-C3: Can a student who lost their key material get a new pseudonym mid-term? This risks bounded double upvotes. Alternatively, is losing participation credit acceptable?
NQ-C4: Can participation continue after level tokens or sharing open (depends on Q18)?
NQ-C5: Is the undetectable risk of a student transferring a verified-level token to another student acceptable for grading (§7.11)?
NQ-C6: On a merge, does a student who upvoted both duplicates keep 2 'upvotes given'?
NQ-C7: Which threshold version determines a student's level: the version at their first participation, the originally published version, or the most favourable version?
NQ-C8: Is 'Still unclear' limited to one per student per answer, and is its count visible to staff?
NQ-C9: Which differencing protection applies to level aggregates once named shares exist?
NQ-C10: Does hiding or deleting content remove its participation credit?
NQ-C11: Is a separate board origin (subdomain) acceptable UX, given the 'explicit anonymity explanations' requirement (§8)?
risks: The user's relayed request was a status question ('what is the privacy agents doing?'), not a request for new work. This run completed the Family C notes in small incremental edits; the file is about 65 KB, a little above the 30-50 KB target.
In a web app the server ships the JavaScript that holds the client secret, so 'even the server cannot link' fails against an active or compromised operator or anyone with deploy-key access.

Host-vendor request logs (IP and timing across the identity and board origins) allow statistical linkage that no cryptographic design here removes. OHTTP needs a non-colluding third-party relay, whose cost and availability are unverified.
Under C1, level tokens can be transferred between colluding students without detection, which is a grade-integrity regression compared with Families A and B.
Device-loss re-issuance creates unlinkable Sybil pseudonyms that break exact one-upvote-per-student. Forbidding re-issuance causes credit loss and support load.
WebAuthn PRF support data conflicts for Safari get() (MDN BCD vs WebKit), so PRF-derived secrets are unreliable across UW devices until tested on real hardware.
The TypeScript libraries (blindrsa-ts 0.4.6, privacypass-ts 0.9.0) are pre-1.0 with no audit statement on their repo pages.
Family C makes the §6.4 exceptional process impossible after the fact. If UW policy requires that process, adopting C1 would force a redesign, which is a corner for production.

factcheck:auth-email.summary:
I fact-checked auth-A1, auth-A2 and other-O1 (the 70 claims in claims-other-1.json plus the budget-relevant rows of each Verification log). The report is at P:/code/_clearcourse-scratch/factcheck/other-1.md and was written in chunks; the notes files were not touched. I did not check on any privacy agent: this run covered only the sign-in, LTI and email notes.

None of the claims was refuted outright. Every price and free-tier limit matched the live pages: Resend, SES, Cloudflare, Postmark, Mailgun, SendGrid, MailerSend, WorkOS, Auth0, Clerk, Supabase and Firebase.

Findings that matter for the recommendations and the <$5/month budget:
1. O1 leaves something out. New AWS accounts on the Free account plan close automatically after 6 months, or sooner if credits run out, unless upgraded. The credits are $100 at sign-up plus up to $100 earned. A public prototype should use the Paid account plan.
2. O1 understates something. New SES accounts start on the Essentials plan ($0.16 per 1,000) from 2026-07-21. The SES pricing page states this outright, but O1 calls it an inference. The "à la carte" proposal means cancelling that default plan; at prototype volume the difference is cents.
3. A1 overstates the NIST session limits. The AAL1 30-day and AAL2 24 h / 1 h idle limits are SHOULD in the standard, not SHALL. Only the ban on email for out-of-band authentication is a SHALL NOT.
4. A2's wording on `kid` is too broad. The Security Framework requires `kid` in key sets, not in every JWT header. A2's body applies it correctly to the tool's JWKS.
5. A1's advisory count needs two corrections. The count of 10 between 26 Jun and 30 Sep is right across all 4 pages, but one of the two Critical advisories is in @better-auth/scim, not sso. Another 9 advisories, including a Critical SSRF in @better-auth/sso, were published on 31 May 2026.
6. Smaller additions:
   - Cloudflare Email preview also stores attachments, which O1 does not mention.
   - The Brightspace LTI article says "D2L does not yet support all aspects of the standard".
   - The Brightspace knowledge-base page still mentions the Anonymous deployment setting. That confirms the author's "conflicting" flag; the API docs say the setting is now always false.
   - D2L "Dynamic Registration disabled by default" means the new registration starts disabled, not that the feature is off.
7. Some claims-file URLs do not back the claim: Postmark prices (they are on /pricing, not eu-privacy), moodle-docker (licence and activity come from the GitHub API, not the Moodle docs page), and the jose push date (GitHub API, not npm). The 1EdTech membership requirement is stated on its page, although the author marked it unverified.

Still unverifiable:
- Whether SES keeps message bodies.
- UW's Entra consent setting.
- UW's LEARN role mapping.
- Brevo's limits (page did not load).
- Whether SES production sending is allowed on the AWS Free plan.
- Claims with no URL: hosted Keycloak costing more than $5/month, and a magic link being used up by a link scanner.

serious: S-A1: Postgres xmin is readable on every cc_web-readable table. It gives an exact global transaction order, which defeats created_at coarsening. Any identity row that is rewritten at activity-correlated moments (for example an OIDC sign-in upsert of identity.users, roster sync, preferences) then joins to content by nearest xid through an ordinary query. Test #13 checks only writes inside the posting transaction. Fix: give cc_web views or functions instead of base-table SELECT, make identity upserts no-ops when nothing changed, and wash content xmin. (System-column visibility is Unverified against the official page.)

S-A2: Variant K3 passes the KEK as a bind parameter on every privileged call, next to the session token and the body. Any parameter-logging path (log_statement or log_min_duration_statement, auto_explain, pgaudit, client-side interpolation by a driver or pooler) would log the master key, the identity token and the content together. Fix: Vault (K2), or compute the HMACs in the app so the key never enters SQL.

S-A3: A level-distribution time series read during term can be differenced against the content timeline, which attributes threshold crossings to specific posts. NQ-A7(a) only hides the distribution once the sharing window opens. Fix: one end-of-term snapshot, or frozen snapshots on a fixed cadence.

S-A4: Mode D credit tokens are bearer tokens kept in localStorage. On a shared device they can be redeemed by the next student, and students can trade them. Fix: bind redemption to the issuing session.
unmet_requirements: §6.2 ordinary queries cannot join: partly met until S-A1 is fixed
§10 Students alone decide whether to share: partly met until S-A3 is fixed
§7.9 credit the right student in Mode D: unmet until S-A4 is fixed
vendor_fact_errors: None found in the facts re-checked. Caveats: Postgres logging defaults are treated as the deployed defaults (the actual vendor values are Unverified), and the claim that K3 keeps the KEK from the DB vendor is weaker than stated because the KEK crosses the DB connection on every call.

serious: S-B1: For 'you upvoted' and the inbox, the BOARD service receives one viewer's tag set for N questions in a single call. Per-item unlinkability therefore holds for the database but fails at the service layer: a BOARD log or compromise can build pseudonymous profiles. Fix: BOARD returns the full tag sets and the Gateway tests membership itself.

S-B2: Receipts are bearer tokens (the browser retries POST /credit {receipt}), so credit can be traded or leaked on shared devices and the verified level may not be the named student's own. Fix: a Gateway MAC that binds the receipt to the cpid.

S-B3: Batching hides time but not action type. Per-cpid deltas within a batch, together with DB-Board buckets and always-on D1 Time Travel, give a cpid-to-authored-questions profile without K_root. The both-dumps attacker is rated 'mostly holds', which is too optimistic. Fix: a per-action-type k rule, or apply credits once a day.

S-B4: The Free-plan 10 ms CPU spike covers only merges, not the email sweep (roster × updated questions) or inbox HMACs. Likely result is Workers Paid at $5/month, and the pressure to consolidate Workers would collapse the separation.
S-B5: A daily-refreshed level histogram still allows day-level differencing, and survey-then-share sequencing is not addressed.
unmet_requirements: §7.9/§7.10 integrity: partly met until S-B2 is fixed
§3 identity-linked discussion analytics: at risk at the BOARD service layer until S-B1 is fixed
vendor_fact_errors: None found. Re-checked D1 limits (10 DBs on Free; 500 MB/10 GB; Time Travel 7/30 days), Workers Logs on by default for new Workers, and Queues on Free (10,000 ops/day, fixed 24 h retention, 3 ops per message). Omission: Cloudflare Observability pricing changes on 2026-12-01.

fatal: F-C1: The recommended hybrid H1 keeps author_pseudonym and reporter_pseudonym = HMAC(K_c, user_id) on every content row, and K_c must be online for every request. The operator, anyone with secrets plus a dump, or a legal order can therefore recover all past question and comment authorship silently, with no approval or audit. That defeats §6.4 'default: nobody can deanonymize' in practice. C also misstates the comparison (it says that under A/B a dump with K_c 'links everything'; authorship is never stored in A/B) and claims K_c can be held k-of-n, which is impossible for an online key. Fix: no author column, per-item tags as in A/B.
serious: S-C1: Per-course pseudonyms on content rows let any Board-store query group a student's whole activity (profiles, §3 activity breakdowns). One identification exposes everything that student did.

S-C2: Level-token issuance (level_token_issued flips for P_c) followed by the named share links the pseudonym to the name through timing or logs, and that exposes the entire authored history. The proposed 'auto-issue for everyone' is not possible with blind signing, and 'wait a day before sharing' can silently fail to carry out a student's decision to share.

S-C3: The 'key structural finding' that exact merge de-duplication requires a linkable per-course pseudonym is overstated. A and B achieve exact merges with per-item tags plus a key-holding roster recompute. Left unqualified in the ADR, it would push the owner toward pseudonym-on-row designs.
S-C4: Integrity regressions in C1: undetectable level-token transfer, Sybil pseudonyms through device-loss re-issuance (double upvotes, §7.7), and credit loss.
S-C5: Under C1, §7.13 targeted email is only partly met (in-app only, or a uniform digest).
unmet_requirements: §6.4 default nobody can deanonymize: unmet in practice for the operator under H1
§3 no individual activity breakdowns / identity-linked analytics: at risk (S-C1)
§7.13 targeted email: partly unmet under C1
§7.7 no double-counting: not guaranteed with C1 re-issuance
§7.10 verified level: not guaranteed with C1 token transfer
vendor_fact_errors: Crypto and library facts correct (blindrsa-ts 0.4.6, Apache-2.0, sjcl 1.0.9). Omission: blindrsa-ts declares node >=24.
Decision-relevant comparative errors: the A/B dump comparison, the k-of-n custody claim for an online key, and the overgeneralised merge 'structural finding'.

cross_cutting: X1: Error-reporting SDK defaults. Sentry's Next.js SDK collects server-side incoming request bodies, the IP and cookies by default, and always sends setUser() data (verified 2026-10-11). One error on POST /questions then puts identity and content in one error report, which §3 forbids. No design names this default.

X2: Level-histogram time-series differencing during term (not just after sharing opens) attributes threshold crossings to posts and narrows candidates once names are shared. Proposed NEW-1: end-of-term snapshot only, or fixed-cadence frozen snapshots.

X3: Survey-then-share sequencing. §7.12 puts the survey before sharing. A new survey response revealed live next to a new named share on the same date links text to name in small classes. Proposed NEW-2: reveal survey results only after the survey closes.
X4: Post-redirect-get. The GET of a brand-new question id right after posting writes the author's IP to host request logs, and auth logs map that IP to a name. Not mentioned by any design.
X5: Live counters and new-question arrival in presentation mode are a classroom observation channel. Show a snapshot instead.
X6: Any impersonation or support tool (Q7) gives per-student access to the session-bound 'my state' oracles, which deanonymizes votes, follows and counts.
X7: Per-event email templates (for example 'Question merged') plus audit-log dates link followers to questions for the email provider plus the operator. Use one generic template.
X8: IP and timing correlation across host, auth and email logs, plus the active operator or host vendor, cannot be fixed under a <$5/month budget. These must be documented limitations (§6.2, §11).
X9: Stylometry, self-identification and small classes: document them. Per-item tags (A/B) avoid giving an attacker a ready-made grouping.
X10: Hide/delete credit and self-upvote blocking need an author link that A and B deliberately lack. Owner decision needed before the Q9 ADR.
X11: Backups, PITR and D1 Time Travel delay the effect of crypto-shredding. X12: mid-term account deletion breaks merge de-dup unless enrolment tombstones are kept.
redteam:privacy.summary:
This answers what the privacy agent was doing. It was the adversarial red-teamer for the three Q9 privacy designs, and that critique is now finished. It is written to P:/code/_clearcourse-scratch/critique/privacy-redteam.md (about 510 lines). Earlier runs of this step had hung on overlong responses; this run wrote the file one section at a time.

I read the three design notes, CONTRIBUTING.md and CLAUDE.md; I did not re-read source-prompt.txt. I re-checked 7 vendor and standard facts against official pages (checked 2026-10-11): Cloudflare Workers Logs, Queues and D1; Postgres system columns; blindrsa-ts on npm; Sentry's Next.js defaults. No vendor-fact errors turned up. Claims I could not confirm are marked Unverified, most importantly who can read the Postgres xmin column through tables and views.

Ratings:
- **A (database-enforced): adequate.** It is the most complete and honest note. Its main gap is that the web app's normal DB role can read xmin (an internal transaction counter) on tables it can see. That would let an ordinary query link a student's sign-in to their post, getting around the timestamp coarsening. Other gaps: in variant K3 the master key is passed in every SQL call; the instructor's level-count view can be compared over time to pin threshold crossings on specific posts; and in its deferred-credit mode, credit tokens can be handed to another student.
- **B (separated services): adequate.** The service that stores questions is sent each viewer's upvote/follow markers in one request, so it can build per-student profiles. Credit receipts can be handed to another student. Batching hides timing but not the kind of action. The Free-plan CPU check leaves out the email sweep, so it probably needs Workers Paid at $5/month.
- **C (cryptographic): weak.** Its recommended hybrid stores an author pseudonym on every question and comment, and the key is online. Whoever holds that key can recover every past author silently, which defeats §6.4. C also overstates its "merges need a linkable pseudonym" finding (A and B already do exact merges without one) and gets the comparison with A/B backwards. Its blind-token exit survey is worth keeping.

Attacks that hit all three designs:
- An error-reporting tool's default settings would put identity and question text in the same error report.
- The level-count view, read repeatedly during term, can be lined up against new posts.
- A student who fills in the survey and then shares their level in one sitting can be linked to their survey text.
- Viewing a brand-new question right after posting it records the author's IP in the host's logs.

There are 7 proposed new open questions (NEW-1 to NEW-7) and a list of actors no design can protect against, for the limitations-of-anonymity document. Suggested direction, for the owner to decide: A's data model and tests, a few of B's ideas, C's survey tokens, plus fixes for the cross-cutting attacks.

research:open-questions.recommendation: Proposal for the owner, not a decision. Adopt WCAG 2.2 AA (Q15), a Markdown threat model in docs/threat-model/ (Q8), and a manual moderation queue with placeholder rate limits and no stored reporter identity (Q20). These are the milestone-1 blockers. Split milestone 1 into 1a (sign-in, admin config, manual card editor, audit, tests) and 1b (board, moderation, presentation, search, private counter), with 1b starting only after the Q9 ADR and threat model exist. Defer sharing, the survey, per-level analytics, the wizard, grading and export, so that Q16, Q18, Q10, Q11 and Q12 do not block the first public prototype. Only the Q16 rule shape (release once after the window closes, with a residual check) goes into the data model now; the default N=10 is a placeholder.

options.name: Q15: WCAG 2.2 AA vs 2.1 AA vs 2.0 AA
options.verdict: Proposal: 2.2 AA. It is a superset of the 2.0 AA legal floor in AODA and UW Policy 58, and W3C recommends using the latest version. Blocks M1: yes.

options.name: Q16: fixed cell size / class minimum / residual check / release after window / banding / noise
options.verdict: Proposal: one release after sharing closes, plus a residual check (at least N non-sharers, not all at one level), plus complementary suppression. Survey responses revealed in one batch, unordered, without timestamps. N=10 is a placeholder. Blocks M1 only if sharing, the survey or level counts ship.

options.name: Q20: per-user vs per-IP vs host WAF limits; manual queue vs auto-hide vs pre-moderation; soft vs hard delete
options.verdict: Proposal: R3 (per-user/course/action for writes, per-IP before sign-in), M1 manual queue, soft delete, reports stored without reporter identity. All numbers are placeholders. Blocks M1 if the board ships.

options.name: Q8: Markdown in repo / tool file / external doc / repo + in-app page
options.verdict: Proposal: Markdown in docs/threat-model/ using STRIDE and LINDDUN, plus an owner-approved in-app limitations page. Blocks M1: yes (§6.3).

options.name: Q14: Postgres INSERT-only table / + hash chain / + locked object storage / logging vendor
options.verdict: Proposal: audit E1 (moderation) and E2 (deanonymization), which the spec requires; E3–E8 for owner approval. Storage L1+L2 (INSERT-only table plus hash chain), with L3 (locked object storage) before any deanonymization. Retention is a placeholder.

options.name: Q17: keep all / per-domain schedule / institution-configurable / prototype wipe
options.verdict: Proposal: prototype wipe (D4) plus per-domain lifecycle hooks for M1; institution-configurable periods (D3) from the UW Privacy office before any UW pilot.

options.name: Q18: manual / dates fixed at policy publication / LMS-derived / term-wide
options.verdict: Proposal: W2+F2. Dates are fixed when the participation policy is published, and export/apply happens only after close. Not needed for M1 if sharing is deferred.

options.name: Q13: none essential / rule-affecting essential / in-app-only essential / per-course
options.verdict: Proposal: N3. Card changes and the sharing-window notice are essential in-app; all email is user-managed; email never contains anonymous content text.

options.name: Q1: config file / minimal admin page / + role management / full multi-tenant
options.verdict: Proposal: A2, a minimal settings page plus an institution table holding the §4 configurables.

options.name: Q7: none / synthetic view-as-role / read-only / full impersonation
options.verdict: Proposal: none (I0), with synthetic previews (I1) optional. Not a blocker if the answer is none.

options.name: Q19: inline strings / externalised English / institution overrides / lang tags on cards / bilingual
options.verdict: Proposal: L1 from day one (cheap), and L3 if WCAG 2.2 AA is adopted (SC 3.1.2). Translations are deferred.

options.name: Q10/Q11/Q12 deferral
options.verdict: All three can be deferred: ship the manual editor, pass/fail only or no grading, and no export. NQ-12a must be answered before sharing ships because export/apply is the trigger that makes shares final.

risks: Differencing: aggregate level counts minus the named shared-results list can reveal non-sharers' levels; a single N threshold does not prevent it (Q16).
Survey-then-share ordering plus timestamps or a live response counter can link written survey answers to a named sharer (Q16/Q18).
Notification emails and follow lists create identity-to-content links in third-party mail systems unless payloads omit content text (Q13, Q9).
Storing reporter identity on reports, or detailed host request logs with precise post times, creates timing and identity side channels (Q20).
INSERT-only Postgres audit tables are not immutable against the table owner; §6.4 'immutable' needs external locked storage before any deanonymization (Q14).
Deleting a student's posts on account removal conflicts with unlinkability; must be designed with Q9 (Q17).
A public prototype with real UW students may trigger UW privacy obligations (Information Risk Assessment, notice, opt-out) before launch (NQ-2a).
Including the board (1b) in milestone 1 makes Q8 and Q9 hard prerequisites; schedule risk if Q9 design is slow.
Several primary legal texts (O. Reg. 191/11, FIPPA Reg. 460, CRTC FAQ) could not be fetched, and the LEARN grade CSV format is unverified.
The CASL reading (notifications are not commercial messages) is an interpretation, not legal advice.

judge:privacy.recommendation: PROPOSAL for the owner (Q9 stays open): adopt "A+", a layered hybrid on design A's single-Postgres core. All five §6.1 domains sit in separate schemas with no cross-domain foreign keys. No content row stores an author, pseudonym, tag or session (P1). Counters are keyed by pid = HMAC(K_pid, user_id), and de-duplication uses per-item keyed tags. The per-course key K_c is stored only wrapped (AES-GCM under a host-held KEK). Unwrapping and every HMAC happen app-side in a server-only linkage module, so no key ever enters SQL (fixes red-team S-A2). No runtime role can SELECT any base table outside `catalog`: reads go through SECURITY DEFINER functions, and identity upserts are no-ops when nothing changed (fixes S-A1, the xmin channel). Functions that carry credit or tags can be called only by a separate `cc_link` login role used solely by the linkage module. No read function takes a viewer's tag list; the app checks membership itself (B's S-B1 fix). Merges re-key tags by recomputing over the roster inside one transaction, and counters are never touched. Crediting is synchronous (Mode S) in the prototype, with an optional daily-batch Mode B that needs no schema change. Notifications are computed on read in-app, and email is one generic, content-free daily digest whose outbox rows are deleted after sending. Askers are not auto-followed. The level distribution is a frozen snapshot on a fixed cadence and is hidden once sharing opens. Survey text is revealed only after the survey closes; C's blind-token survey is kept as an upgrade. Crypto-shredding at end of term is an option (Q17). Scores: A+ 83.5, A 74.5, B-full 67.0, B-lite 66.5, C-H1 65.0, C1 53.5. B-full only wins if protection against the operator carries about a third of all weight (PQ-P1). The document also holds the threat-model outline, an 18-item limitations list, 22 controls, 36 negative tests and a verification log (14 pages re-fetched; checked date recorded as 2026-10-11).

ranking.option: A+ (A plus red-team fixes, with grafts from B and C)
ranking.rationale: Meets every REQUIRED-tier property (ordinary queries including system columns, staff, logs, exports, identifiers, non-sharers' levels) once S-A1 to S-A4 and X1 to X7 are applied. Most locks become CI catalogue assertions. Fits plain managed Postgres under the stack judge's ~USD 1.17/month proposal. About 18 to 25 sessions (unmeasured).

Same strong data model and the cheapest build (13 to 17 sessions), but it has an ordinary-query xmin channel (S-A1), passes the KEK as a bind parameter so it can reach DB logs (S-A2), and its level time series leaks non-sharers' levels (S-A3).

Removes the SQL join class structurally and is strongest against holders of only some stores. Costs about 29 to 39 sessions across roughly 8 DBs and 9 services. Workers Free CPU risk pushes toward the USD 5 paid minimum. Still has the BOARD tag-set leak (S-B1), bearer receipts (S-B2) and per-type batch deltas (S-B3).
Fewer services, but one Gateway credential holds identity, shared results and the notification sweep, so most of B's operator gain is lost while much of its complexity remains.

ranking.option: C-H1 (server pseudonym stored on content rows)
ranking.rationale: Anyone holding K_c can silently recover the authorship of every question and comment (F-C1), and any Board reader can GROUP BY a per-student profile (S-C1). Only its blind-token survey and dump-diff test are worth keeping.

Strongest against stored-data holders, but targeted email (§7.13) is partly unmet, Sybil re-issue can double-count upvotes (§7.7), level tokens are transferable (§7.10, §7.11), it corners the §6.4 option, and key-recovery UX is the hardest part for a solo developer.

must_haves: No author, pid, tag, session, IP or UA column on any anonymous table, enforced by a per-table column allow-list (C-01, T-02)
No runtime role has SELECT on any base table outside catalog; reads only through definer functions; a test proves cc_web cannot read xmin or ctid (C-02, T-01, T-21)
Identity and roster upserts are no-ops when unchanged; auth-library session refresh disabled and the session table readable only by cc_auth (C-09, T-24)
Keys only app-side: wrapped K_c readable only via cc_link, KEK only in the host secret store, no key material in SQL, settings or logs (C-06, T-17)
Credit- and tag-bearing definers callable only by the cc_link role of the linkage module; no read function accepts a viewer's tag list (C-07, C-08)
ENABLE plus FORCE RLS on locked tables; definers have search_path pinned and PUBLIC EXECUTE revoked in the creating transaction; no BYPASSRLS on any cc_* role (C-03 to C-05)

Logging invariants (log_statement none, log_min_duration_statement -1, log_parameter_max_length_on_error 0, track_commit_timestamp off, ORM logger off), tested through the production driver and pooler (T-07, T-33)
No third-party error, analytics or replay SDK on routes that receive anonymous content unless NEW-4 approves explicit settings (Sentry collects request bodies and IP by default)
UUIDv4 only, no ids in query strings, no post-redirect GET of a newly created id (C-13)
Level distribution as frozen snapshots, suppressed below N and hidden once sharing opens; survey revealed only after close; presentation-mode snapshots (C-16)
One generic content-free email template, daily digest, outbox rows deleted after send, no auto-follow on asking (C-17, C-18)
Enrolment tombstones until seal so merges stay exact (C-19); merge property test (T-11)
Threat model and limitations-of-anonymity document (§5 outline, 18 items) written before any content or participation code (§6.3)
risks: The operator, host and DB vendors stay inside the trust boundary: with full data plus the KEK, upvote, follow and report sets and per-student counts can be reconstructed. This is a documented limitation, not engineered away.
Mode S leaves an operator-level xmin link between a content row and the counter row until the student's next action or the nightly wash. How much the wash actually helps is Unverified.
Whether system columns can be reached through definer functions or views, and whether Better Auth can suppress ipAddress/userAgent, are Unverified and need spikes T-21 and T-24 before the ADR.
No author link means credit for hidden spam cannot be revoked and self-upvotes cannot be blocked unless the owner accepts a P1 weakening (PQ-P2, PQ-P3).
One app process holds every DB credential, so an app-server compromise defeats the cc_link role separation (S-tier).
Build estimate of about 18 to 25 sessions is unmeasured; PL/pgSQL definers and catalogue discipline need care on every migration.
Crypto-shredding only takes effect after vendor backup and WAL copies expire, and vendor-internal retention is Unverified.
Merge recomputation timing at realistic roster sizes is Unverified (T-31).

research:design-a11y.recommendation: PROPOSAL for the owner, to approve via an ADR: build the UI from shadcn/ui source and Tailwind CSS v4 on React Aria primitives, with Base UI as the fallback. Run a short spike first, because shadcn's style/base choice cannot be changed after init. All styling would come from our own three-layer CSS-custom-property tokens. Admin brand colours would pass through a server-side WCAG contrast guardrail (UW gold pairs accessibly only with black). Fonts would be open-licence and self-hosted. No UW or D2L fonts, logos or BrightspaceUI components would be used, and GOV.UK patterns would be borrowed for tags, question pages and error summaries. Propose WCAG 2.2 AA for Q15, checked by axe via Playwright in CI plus a manual NVDA/VoiceOver/zoom/forced-colours checklist. Passing axe should never be presented as conformance.

research:testing.recommendation: PROPOSAL (owner decides; conditional on the Q3 and Q9 ADRs): use Vitest 5 for unit, property, DB and API tests, with fast-check, against a real Postgres (a GitHub Actions service container in CI, Testcontainers locally; PGlite is not used for anything that depends on roles). Add SQL catalog assertions, with pgTAP optional, and Playwright with @axe-core/playwright. Build a canary co-occurrence scanner that checks UI DOM and RSC payloads, API bodies and headers, exports, app and Postgres logs, and traces. Generate a role x endpoint matrix from the route list, deny-by-default. Add dependency-cruiser boundary rules and StrykerJS scoped to privacy modules, run on a schedule. Everything runs on GitHub Actions Free (2,000 private-repo minutes, blocked rather than billed when no payment method is on file), and every §10 criterion maps to named tests (§5.5 of the note).

new_open_questions: PNQ-T1: Should mandatory negative tests also cover institutional admins and operators? §9 names only instructors and TAs.
PNQ-T2: Scanner strictness: any identity canary next to any content canary, or only a student next to their own content? May a student's own view show 'you asked this'?
PNQ-T3: What is the exact list of TA permissions an instructor can assign (§5 gives only examples)?
PNQ-T4: Which survey metadata is 'necessary' (§7.12), e.g. is a submission date kept, and at what granularity?
PNQ-T5: What does 'preserve all comments where reasonable' (§7.7) mean for merge tests?
PNQ-T6: Private or public repository (affects free CI minutes and runner size)?
PNQ-T7: Is an external security/privacy/accessibility review wanted before production?
PNQ-T8: Any required coverage or mutation-score threshold, or none?
PNQ-T9: Should the negative suite also run against a deployed preview (synthetic data) to catch platform log/cache leaks?
PNQ-T10: Retention period for CI artefacts (traces, logs) containing synthetic canaries.
PNQ-T11: Is a read-only post-deploy catalog self-check against production acceptable, and with which credentials?
risks: The test suite could itself create the forbidden mapping if the seed oracle (who wrote what) is persisted to DB, fixtures, logs or CI artifacts. It must stay in test-process memory only.
PGlite or mocks used for role/RLS tests could give false confidence; privacy tests must run on a real Postgres server.
Using information_schema.view_table_usage for the no-cross-domain-view check silently misses tables not owned by the current role.
Default Postgres error logging records failing statement text; any non-parameterised query with content text leaks it into the DB log.
UUIDv7 or sequential ids would embed creation time or order and enable timing correlation; tests must assert v4 only.
Tool version drift: Vitest 5 is new, and Stryker's vitest-runner is only dev-tested on Vitest 4.1; spike before adopting.
CI minute estimates are unmeasured; nightly E2E plus mutation runs could approach the 2,000-minute quota on a private repo.
A §10 map cannot be completed for sign-in and provisioning until Q4 and Q5 are answered; those tests are placeholders.
Automated a11y and authz tests catch only part of the problems (Playwright and OWASP both say so); manual review is still needed.
